samples.summary: Scope creep: the 401 redirect-latch timer in `fetchWithAuth` is unrelated to the issue's acceptance criteria. The task plan (docs/tasks/active/20260916-nav-guard-unsent-edits-todo.md) and the issue's six acceptance criteria are entirely about in-app route changes; none mentions session eviction. The latch release (`REDIRECT_LATCH_MS`, a 2s timer, plus a new test file `tests/api/auth.test.ts`) changes auth behaviour for every 401 path in the app and is only tangentially motivated by the *pre-existing* `beforeunload` guard, not by anything this PR adds. It is a defensible fix but belongs in its own change; bundled here it enlarges the blast radius of a UI PR into session handling.
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260916-nav-guard-unsent-edits-todo.md lines 79-86 list the acceptance criteria; none covers the 401 redirect. The diff adds REDIRECT_LATCH_MS + timer to src/api/auth.ts.

samples.summary: The design doc now elevates "an app-issued redirect must be a `replace`" to an app-wide invariant (docs/design/sync-status.md: "an invariant this app has to uphold, not a property it happens to have"), and the provider's correctness for expired sessions depends on it — yet nothing enforces it. `<Navigate>` defaults to a push, so a future `<Navigate to="/login" />` added anywhere silently routes an eviction redirect through the guard, where a "Stay" strands the user in a route their session no longer reaches. There is no lint rule (no `no-restricted-syntax` in the frontend eslint config), no architecture test, and the new test suite only covers today's call sites. Today all ten `<Navigate>` uses do pass `replace`, so nothing is broken now — the cost is regression risk, hence minor.
samples.evidence: Grepped `<Navigate` across packages/frontend/src: 10 sites, all with `replace` after this diff. Grepped frontend eslint configs for `Navigate`/`no-restricted-syntax`: no matches.

samples.summary: The Goals section now reads "Leaving a document that holds unpushed edits requires a deliberate confirmation — closing or reloading the tab, and navigating away inside the app", which is stated more broadly than what ships: browser back/forward (a `POP`) arrives on the history listener, below the navigator the guard wraps, and is explicitly left uncovered in Risks. A Goal that the same document's Risks section contradicts is the kind of overclaim this repo's design docs otherwise avoid (compare the careful hedging on offline persistence). Suggest scoping the Goal to app-initiated navigation.
samples.evidence: docs/design/sync-status.md Goals (lines 35-37) vs. the revised Risks entry "**Browser back/forward is not guarded.**"

samples.summary: The `fetchWithAuth` 401 eviction latch is documented inside sync-status.md's navigation-guard section. Session eviction is an auth concern owned by docs/design/backend.md ("auth system"); folding an auth-behaviour change into the sync-status doc because the beforeunload guard makes the redirect refusable files it by cause rather than by subsystem, and a future reader of the auth path will not look here. A one-line cross-reference from the auth doc would fix it.
samples.evidence: docs/design/sync-status.md paragraph beginning "The router is not the only eviction path…" describes packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts behaviour.
